text: A pittance is an amount of money so small that it is close to an insult, and it describes what someone is paid or what something sold for, not what you pay for a thing. Saying Shein's suppliers stitch for a pittance is the article's answer to how a blouse can cost $3: the people sewing them earn very little.

Something conspicuous stands out and cannot be missed, so conspicuously marks a thing that is unusually noticeable. It hits hardest attached to an absence, as here: a prospectus describes a business in huge detail, so one that says almost nothing about moving factories out of China is silent in a way readers notice.

Precipitous comes from precipice, meaning a cliff edge, and it means steep and sudden. You meet it far more often describing a falling number than actual ground: investors bought into Shein when it was valued at $100bn and are watching it list at a reported $27bn, a drop fast enough that the company has had to pay them settlements.

Novel here is the adjective, meaning new and original, not the noun meaning a book. Shein's novel business model was new in the way it worked, using data to spot trends and turning them into designs within days. The related noun is novelty.

Proved usually means demonstrated beyond doubt, but in the phrase proved a hit it carries a different and very common sense: turned out to be. The model proved a hit in Western markets means it turned out to be popular there, with no proving involved.

In business writing a market is not a place where you buy vegetables. It means all the customers for something, usually in one region, so Western markets means the shoppers of North America and Europe. A company entering a new market is starting to sell to a new set of people.

To deteriorate is to get steadily worse. It works for a physical thing, like a roof that deteriorates, and for a situation or a run of numbers, as here, where Shein's sales growth and its profits both got worse year after year.

Wares is an old word for goods offered for sale, still alive in phrases like selling their wares. Saying Shein does not sell its wares in China is a slightly formal way of noting that it has clothes made there but does not offer them to Chinese shoppers.

To be perturbed is to be bothered or unsettled by something. Customers who are not perturbed by the occasionally shoddy quality are people the poor quality does not trouble enough to stop them ordering again.

Shoddy means badly made, cheap in the bad sense. The word first named a cloth woven from shredded old wool, which is how it came to mean poor quality, an origin that sits oddly well in an article about fast fashion.

Mounting means growing or piling up, and it attaches almost only to bad things: mounting debts, mounting pressure, mounting troubles. The word tells you Shein's problems are not merely present but increasing.

In business an offering is simply a product or service a company puts on sale. Amazon's own ultra-cheap offering means the cheap shopping service Amazon launched, called Haul. Nothing is being given away.

A loophole is a gap in a rule that lets you legally avoid what the rule was meant to do. Nobody broke the law by mailing parcels under the de minimis limit, which is exactly what makes it a loophole rather than smuggling, and governments close loopholes by rewriting the rule.

A duty here is not a responsibility. It is a tax a government charges on goods entering the country, collected at the border before the shipment is released. Packages imported free of duties crossed into America without that tax being charged.

To levy a tax is to impose it and collect it, and the word is used almost only about governments. Higher tariffs levied by the second Trump administration means tariffs that administration imposed on goods arriving from China.

To diversify is to spread out so you do not depend on any one thing. Shein diversifying its manufacturing base means arranging for clothes to be made in more than one country, so a tariff or a rule change in one place cannot halt everything at once.

An arm of an organisation is one of its divisions. Reliance is a huge Indian company spanning many businesses, and its retail arm is the part that runs shops and sells to ordinary customers, which is the part Shein went into partnership with.

A conglomerate is one company that owns businesses in unrelated industries. Reliance sells petrol, runs a mobile network and operates supermarkets under a single owner, which is what makes it a conglomerate rather than simply a retailer.

To antagonise someone is to annoy them into hostility, and it shares a root with antagonist, the character who opposes the hero. Wanting to avoid antagonising Chinese officials means Shein would rather not advertise that work is leaving China and turn the government against it.

Alleged means claimed but not proved, and journalists use it to report an accusation without endorsing it. The alleged use of forced labour means people have accused Shein of it while Shein denies it, and the article is not telling you which side is right.

Bless usually belongs to religion, but in politics and business it means to give official approval. China's government failed to bless the London option means Beijing never gave the go-ahead, and without it the plan could not proceed.

A settlement is money paid to end a dispute without a court deciding who was right. Shein paying settlements to investors means it paid people whose stake lost value rather than fight them, which is what a company usually does when it would rather not argue in public just before selling shares.

In American usage an administration is a president's government and the officials appointed to run it, named after the president: the second Trump administration means his government in his second term. Britain would call the same thing a government.

A mere in front of a number means only that much, and signals that the writer thinks it small or disappointing. Sales increased by a mere 1% invites you to set that against the 21% growth two years earlier.

Year on year means compared with the same period twelve months earlier, not with the previous quarter. Growth of 1% year on year in the first quarter of 2026 is measured against the first quarter of 2025, which strips out the fact that shoppers spend more in some seasons than others.

To sound someone out is to test their reaction quietly before committing to anything. Shein spent years sounding out various potential stock markets, meaning it was privately asking exchanges and regulators whether a listing would be welcome, without announcing a decision.

To flirt with an idea is to explore it seriously without committing to it. Shein flirted with a London listing, meaning it went far enough to obtain the British regulator's approval and then did not go through with it.

To keep a close eye on something is to watch it carefully because you may need to act. Chinese officials keeping a close eye on Shein's digital operations means they are monitoring how much of the company's data and technology work now runs from outside China.

To go public is to sell shares in your company to ordinary investors for the first time, so anyone can buy a piece of it on a stock exchange. Until then the company is private, owned by a small group, which is what Shein has been through all these years of choosing an exchange.

A stock exchange is a regulated marketplace where shares in companies are bought and sold, like those in New York, London and Hong Kong. A company wanting its shares traded on one must satisfy that exchange and that country's regulator, and must publish detailed information about itself.

A listing is the arrangement that gets a company's shares traded on a particular stock exchange. Which exchange a company picks matters because each brings different rules, different investors and, as this story shows, different politics.

A valuation is what a whole company is judged to be worth. For a private company it comes from what investors paid in the latest round of funding, which is where the $100bn of 2022 came from; once shares trade publicly, buyers and sellers set it, and Shein's is expected to open near $27bn.

Private investors here are firms that buy stakes in companies whose shares are not traded on any exchange. General Atlantic, an American investment firm, bought into Shein this way in 2022, at the $100bn valuation the article keeps returning to.

Revenue is the total money customers pay a company, before a single cost is subtracted. Shein's $42bn of revenue in 2025 is what its clothes sold for, not what it kept, which is how a company can post a huge revenue figure and still be losing money.

Net profit is what remains of revenue once every cost is taken out: suppliers, shipping, salaries, advertising and tax. Shein's net profit of $3.4bn in 2024 is the money the business actually kept that year, and it is the number that has since gone below zero.

Operating at a loss means the costs of running the business came to more than the money it took in, so the year ends below zero rather than above it. A company can do this for a while by spending cash that investors handed it earlier, but not forever.

A prospectus is the long document a company must publish before selling shares to the public, setting out its finances, its business and its risks. It is written under legal rules that punish false statements, which is why the article treats its numbers as solid and finds its silences worth pointing out.

The de minimis rule let a parcel below a set value cross the border with no import duty charged, on the reasoning that collecting a few cents costs more than it raises. The name is from a Latin phrase meaning the law does not concern itself with the smallest things, and in America the threshold was $800, high enough that nearly every Shein parcel slipped under it.

A tariff is a tax on imported goods, set as a percentage of their value and paid as they enter the country. Governments use tariffs both to raise money and to make foreign goods dearer than local ones, and higher American tariffs on Chinese goods are one of the two changes that hit Shein at the same moment.

A supply chain is the whole sequence that turns raw material into a product in your hands: the cotton, the factory that stitches it, the shipping, the delivery. Questions about Shein's supply chain are questions about who made the clothes and under what conditions.

Forced labour means work people are made to do under threat or without being free to leave. It is banned under international law and, for imported goods, under American law, so the accusation that Shein's suppliers used it was serious enough to end the New York listing plan even though Shein denies it.

A regulator is a government body with legal power over an industry, such as the British financial regulator that decides whether a company may sell shares to the public there. Shein obtained its approval in April last year, so the London listing was possible on the British side; what stopped it came from the Chinese government instead.

Temu is the cheap online marketplace that PDD, a Chinese e-commerce group, launched in America in 2022, selling everything from phone cases to furniture at very low prices. It is the clearest of the copycats the article blames for Shein's slowing sales.

Reliance is one of India's largest companies, with businesses in oil, telecoms and retail. Its partnership with Shein means clothes can be made in India rather than only in China, which is what diversifying the manufacturing base looks like in practice.
